title: Working with Alfred Newman on Stormy Weather
summary: Carter arranged source music for singers like Lena Horne and admired music director Alfred Newman.

blocks.x: THE SMITHSONIAN INSTITUTION

Oral History
Benny Carter

Cassettes 3-4
October 13-14, 1976

PRO-TYPISTS, INC.
PROFESSIONAL TRANSCRIPTION SERVICE
AREA CODE 202 347-5395
PROCEEDINGS
... we're continuing this discussion of your first work in films, which was in 1943 -- late in the year, in the film, "Stormy Weather" in which Fats Waller Franz Walla (PHONETIC) played.
The man through whom you became associated with this film was Irving Mills, but who was the musical director of the whole show itself?
Alfred Newman.
Alfred Newman.
Yes.
And this is a man, of course, who you associated with to some considerable degree over many years.
Yes. Right.
Did you hit it off with him right away?

I thought so, yes. He was a very, very kind man -- a man for whom I had a great deal of respect and admiration. He was what I considered a super musician, and he had had a great deal of experience in the field of, you know, scoring for films.
Uh huh. And your -- at this time, you still had your band.
Yes. Uh huh.
Were you actually playing dates while you were doing the work in the film?
Actually, while I was working on the film, we were playing at the Billy Berg Swing Billie Burke Street Club. For Billy Berg.
The Billie Burke. Do you remember exactly what you did in the film? You played on the sound track a little bit, and you arranged some numbers?
I made a number of the arrangements, yes.
Uh huh. Did you score anything in background music, or did you only arrange tunes that the musicians presumably on screen were playing?
Well, not only that they were on screen, playing, but ... now let me get this straight, when you say only on the screen, what do you mean?
Well, I don't really know myself.
Yeah, well that's what we usually call source music.
Source music, uh huh.
But I did no background scoring as far as composition was concerned, if that's what I think you meant. No, I didn't do that.
But then the arrangements that you made were of well known tunes?
Oh, yes ... yes.
Like, what was it -- "Ain't Misbehavin'" ...
"Ain't Misbehavin'," "Can't Give You Anything But Love, things like that.
These were tunes that the musicians were playing in the film -- is that right?
The singers were doing those -- singers like Lena Horne's songs, you know.
Right. And you were arranging those already well known tunes for the band and the singers?
That's right.

Right. I see. What was your impression at that time? Did you say, suddenly -- did a light go on and did you say something like, "Gee, Hollywood! That's great." Or was it more or less the same thing as writing for a band or a singer which you had done for many years?
Well, it was pretty much the same thing ... only different, you know?
Yeah.
And paid much more.
Yes, that made it different.
That made it quite considerably different.
